newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EC demands Italian action on digital phone rules.
newsitem.headline: EC demands Italian action on digital phone rules.

text.p: European Commissioner Karel Van Miert has called on Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi to implement measures to create equal conditions in Italy's digital GSM telephone market, a commission source said.
The source said Van Miert had written to Prodi asking him to fix a precise date for the introduction of the changes, which were drawn up by the Commission in October 1995.
The measures were meant to be introduced by the Italian government in January 1996 to establish a fair market for Italy's second mobile telephone group Omnitel.
"The failure to adopt these measures has had serious consequences for the GSM sector," the letter said.
Omnitel, an international consortium controlled by Olivetti, launched its GSM mobile phone service in December 1995 to compete with state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).
"I especially deplore the failure to apply two corrective measures," Van Miert's letter said.
The first of these was a reduction in the connection fees Omnitel has to pay for access to state-controlled telephone lines, which was meant to save the company some 60 billion lire in 1996-97.
The second was legislation designed to allow Omnitel to set up its own telephone infrastructure, giving the firm its own frequencies for radio bridges.
Van Miert was assured by Italian Telecommunications and Post Minister Antonio Maccanico last September that Italy would implement the measures as fast as possible.
